## Corner Framing

Foreground corner pieces (trees, walls, rocks) layered over the world. They change with the area the hero is in: castle stone in the court, snowy pines at the gate, and a dedicated set for each outdoor biome. **Status: proposal, not implemented yet.**

## At a glance

- **Desktop:** bottom-corner clusters with parallax and a cross-fade between areas.
- **Mobile:** no parallax. A thin top frame in portrait and side strips in landscape, so the thumb stick and attack/skill buttons stay clear.
- **Phase 1:** `court` + `snow` (8 files). **Phase 2:** five outdoor biomes (20 files).
title: Environment

markdown:
Foreground corner framing (trees, walls, rocks) sits on top of the Stronghold world and changes with the area the hero is standing in. **Status: proposal, not implemented yet.**

## Reference

The desktop mockup frames the scene with blurred snowy pines in the bottom-left and bottom-right corners.

![Desktop mockup: snowy pine clusters frame the bottom-left and bottom-right corners](/api/rooms/DR2acdbf9c7c4af10516c89541/attachments/DA522af51364879138364af8a8)

## Concept

Generated concept of the snow area outside the gate. The pines in the bottom corners are the target look for the `snow` corner set: dark blue-toned, snow-laden, softly out of focus, and kept clear of the HUD, skill bar and XP bar.

![Concept: Ember Warden fighting at the Stronghold gate, framed by snowy pines in the bottom corners](/api/rooms/DR7f0a660e4dfc6ca5002753b3/attachments/DA09f0b9e6d337117fec3f3fad)

## Design decisions

1. **Corners follow the area.** The left and right corners match the area under the hero and cross-fade when it changes.
2. **The castle interior has its own set.** `court` wins over any outdoor area. Walking through the gate is the main transition: castle stone gives way to snowy pines.
3. **Desktop gets full parallax.** Bottom corner clusters move slightly faster than the world, with an optional second branch layer for extra depth.
4. **Mobile gets area corners without parallax.**
   - At phone size the clamped offset (±24 px) is barely visible but still costs compositing.
   - The bottom corners are taken by the thumb stick (left) and attack/skills (right).
   - On mobile the job is to signal the current area, and a cross-fade does that.
   - Portrait uses a thin top frame instead of bottom clusters; landscape uses thin side strips.

## Areas

| Area | Corner content | Phase |
|---|---|---|
| `court` (inside the walls) | Stone pillars, wall corners, banners, barrels and crates, warm torch light | 1 |
| `snow` (gate and outskirts) | Snow-laden pines and spruce, cold blue shadows, faint warm rim light | 1 |
| `relic-forest` | Dense deciduous trees, moss, plum-toned roots | 2 |
| `swamp` | Reeds, dead mossy trees, low mist | 2 |
| `mountains` | Cliff rocks, stunted pines | 2 |
| `ash-frontier` | Charred trees, embers, ash | 2 |
| `river` | Riverbank shrubs, wet stones | 2 |

## Art direction

- Painterly style that matches the mockup and the concept above.
- Corners are darker and lower in contrast than the playfield, so they read as foreground and never compete with the hero.
- Depth-of-field blur is painted into the artwork rather than added with CSS.
- Left and right pieces have different silhouettes. Never mirror one side to make the other.
title: Corner Framing — Design & Art Direction

markdown:
The files needed for each area's corner set. See the design and art direction sub-page for the look.

## Format

- Transparent WebP, painterly, matching the mockup.
- Depth-of-field blur painted in, so phones don't pay for a CSS `filter`.
- Sizes are @2x. Pieces are cropped by the screen edge on their outer sides.

## Files per area

| File | Size (@2x) | Used on | Shape |
|---|---|---|---|
| `corner-{area}-left.webp` | ~640×760 | Desktop | Bottom-left cluster |
| `corner-{area}-right.webp` | ~640×760 | Desktop | Bottom-right cluster, different silhouette |
| `corner-{area}-left-mobile.webp` | ~360×300 | Mobile | Top-left frame piece (hanging branches, stone lintel, …) |
| `corner-{area}-right-mobile.webp` | ~360×300 | Mobile | Top-right frame piece |

Optional desktop depth layer: `branch-{area}-left.webp` and `branch-{area}-right.webp` (~420×300).

## Count

| Scope | Areas | Files |
|---|---|---|
| Phase 1 | `court`, `snow` | 8 |
| Phase 2 | `relic-forest`, `swamp`, `mountains`, `ash-frontier`, `river` | 20 |
| Total | 7 | 28 (plus optional branch layers) |
title: Corner Framing — Asset Spec

markdown:
How the corner layer resolves the current area, swaps artwork and follows the camera.

## Current state in code

- **No parallax layer exists.** The edge trees are ordinary `foreground` props from [src/stronghold/terrain.ts](/organizations/ORd5dd6f99b4308d6187031557/repositories/RPe11327fbfe413dbeba246526/files?file=src%2Fstronghold%2Fterrain.ts) (tiles with u/v ≥ 15), so they move 1:1 with the world.
- **The Stronghold scene has one biome (snow).** There is no `biomeAt()` in `src/stronghold/`.
- **The court already has a check.** `inSafeZone()` in [src/stronghold/safe-zone.ts](/organizations/ORd5dd6f99b4308d6187031557/repositories/RPe11327fbfe413dbeba246526/files?file=src%2Fstronghold%2Fsafe-zone.ts) is true on the court side of the gate.
- **The expedition map has 5 biomes.** [src/expedition/world.ts](/organizations/ORd5dd6f99b4308d6187031557/repositories/RPe11327fbfe413dbeba246526/files?file=src%2Fexpedition%2Fworld.ts) derives them from elevation and moisture.

## Flow

```d2
direction: right
hero: Hero tile (u, v)
resolve: "biomeAt(u, v)"
court: court
snow: snow
outer: outdoor biome (noise)
hyst: "Hysteresis (~1.5 s / ~2 tiles)"
swap: "Slot B loads set, cross-fade, swap A/B"
desk: "Desktop: parallax offset + clamp"
mob: "Mobile: static frame"
hero -> resolve
resolve -> court: inSafeZone
resolve -> snow: near gate
resolve -> outer: elsewhere
court -> hyst
snow -> hyst
outer -> hyst
hyst -> swap: area changed
swap -> desk
swap -> mob
```

## Area resolution

New `biomeAt(u, v)` in `src/stronghold/`:

1. `inSafeZone()` → `court`
2. Inside the gate and outskirts radius → `snow`
3. Otherwise → the same noise and seed as `src/expedition/world.ts`, so it matches the expedition map

- **Hysteresis:** switch only after the hero has spent ~1.5 s or ~2 tiles in the new area, so borders don't flicker.
- **Border blend (optional):** each side samples ~6 tiles toward its own side, so an approaching forest appears on that side first.

## Layer — `src/stronghold/parallax.ts`

- A `<div class="fg-parallax">` above the world and below the HUD, with `pointer-events: none`.
- Two slots per side (A/B). On an area change, slot B loads the new set and cross-fades in over 600–800 ms with a slight rise. Then the slots swap roles.
- `<picture>` with `<source media="(max-width: 700px)">` picks the mobile artwork.
- Preload neighbouring sets as the hero approaches and unload distant ones (this matters on mobile).

## Camera hook (desktop only)

- In `draw()` in [src/stronghold/world-view.ts](/organizations/ORd5dd6f99b4308d6187031557/repositories/RPe11327fbfe413dbeba246526/files?file=src%2Fstronghold%2Fworld-view.ts), next to `hero.place(x, y, scale)`, call `parallax.place(cx, cy, scale)`.
- Offset = `-(cx - anchor) * scale * (factor - 1)`, with factor ≈ 1.3 for trees and 1.5 for branches, clamped to ±60 px.
- Move with `translate3d` only (GPU, no repaint), as `snowLayer` does, and set `will-change: transform`.

## Responsive layout

| Viewport | Placement | Size | Motion |
|---|---|---|---|
| Desktop | Bottom-left and bottom-right | `width: clamp(220px, 22vw, 380px)` | Parallax and cross-fade |
| Mobile portrait (≤ 700 px) | Top-left and top-right frame, clear of the clock and HUD | `width: 18vw; max-height: 16dvh` | Cross-fade only |
| Mobile landscape (`max-height: 500px`) | Thin left and right strips, away from the controls | Narrow strip | Cross-fade only |

## Gameplay safety and accessibility

- When the hero or an enemy is on screen inside a corner's bounding box, fade that corner to about 0.5 opacity.
- `prefers-reduced-motion`: no parallax offset, instant swap or a short fade.
- Thin out the existing u/v ≥ 15 foreground spruce props so trees aren't doubled.
title: Corner Framing — Implementation

markdown:
## Verification

- Screenshots at 1440×900, 390×844 and 844×390, taken in the court, at the gate and in the snow outskirts.
- Corners never cover the thumb stick, attack/skill buttons, skill bar, XP bar, clock or HUD.
- Crossing the gate cross-fades court ↔ snow exactly once, with no flicker when walking back and forth on the border.
- Mobile FPS measured with the layer on and off.
- Reduced-motion mode shows no camera-driven movement.

## Open items

- Confirm the phase 1 scope (`court` + `snow`).
- Confirm that mobile keeps the static top frame (portrait) and side strips (landscape).
- Rename the Indonesian biome strings in `src/expedition/world.ts` (`Sungai`, `Pegunungan`, `Rawa`, …) to English before they reach any UI.
